lessons.title: The AI Filmmaking Revolution
lessons.subtitle: Why now is the golden era for AI video creators

cards.headline: A New Kind of Filmmaker
cards.body: For the first time in history, one person with a laptop can produce video that rivals studio-level production. No camera, no crew, no six-figure budget.

cards.headline: The Democratisation of Video
cards.body: AI video tools have collapsed the barrier to entry. What once required a RED camera, colour grading suite, and months of post-production now takes minutes with the right prompt.
bullets: Text-to-video generation in seconds
Consistent characters across scenes
Cinematic camera movements on demand
Professional-grade audio synthesis
cards.statLabel: Cost reduction vs traditional video production using AI tools

cards.headline: Why This Matters Now
cards.body: Brands are desperate for video content — social platforms prioritise it, conversion rates soar with it, and attention spans demand it. But traditional production is slow and expensive. AI filmmakers fill this gap.
bullets: 82% of internet traffic is video
Short-form video has 2.5× higher engagement
Brands need 10× more video than they can produce traditionally

cards.headline: The Opportunity Window
cards.body: We're in the early-adopter phase. Most businesses haven't caught on yet. AI filmmakers who build portfolios now will be the go-to experts when demand explodes.
cards.statLabel: Average project fee for AI video creators with a strong portfolio

cards.headline: Your First Step
cards.body: Write down 3 types of video you'd love to create (short film, brand ad, YouTube content, music video, etc.). This becomes your creative north star for the course.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason AI filmmaking is accessible to individuals now?
options: AI tools eliminate the need for expensive equipment and crews
Social media is easier to use
quiz.explanation: AI video tools remove the need for cameras, crews, and expensive post-production — one person with a laptop can produce cinematic content.

quiz.question: AI video tools can reduce production costs by up to 90% compared to traditional methods.
quiz.explanation: AI eliminates the need for physical equipment, large crews, studio rental, and lengthy post-production workflows, cutting costs dramatically.

quiz.question: What percentage of internet traffic is video content?
quiz.explanation: 82% of internet traffic is now video, making it the dominant content format and creating massive demand for video creators.

lessons.title: Your AI Video Toolkit
lessons.subtitle: Overview of Sora, Runway, Kling, Pika, and when to use each

cards.headline: The Right Tool for the Right Shot
cards.body: There's no single "best" AI video tool. Each excels at different things — and the smart filmmaker knows which to reach for.

cards.headline: Sora (OpenAI)
cards.body: The heavyweight for photorealistic, long-form generation. Sora excels at complex scenes with multiple subjects, realistic physics, and extended motion.
bullets: Best for: Photorealistic scenes, complex camera moves
Strength: Long clips (up to 60s), coherent motion
Weakness: Slower generation, higher cost per clip
Use when: You need the most realistic output possible

cards.headline: Runway Gen-3 & Kling
cards.body: The workhorses for creative production. Runway offers the best image-to-video pipeline, while Kling delivers impressive motion and character consistency.
bullets: Runway: Best image-to-video, motion brush control
Kling: Superior character consistency, longer clips
Both: Fast generation, good for iteration
Use when: Rapid prototyping and creative exploration
cards.statLabel: Average generation time for a 5-second Runway clip

cards.headline: Pika, Luma & Specialists
cards.body: Niche tools that punch above their weight. Pika excels at stylised/animated content. Luma Dream Machine handles 3D-aware scenes. Hailuo offers free high-quality generation.
bullets: Pika: Best for stylised, animated, or surreal content
Luma: 3D-aware generation, great spatial understanding
Hailuo: Free tier with surprisingly good quality
Tip: Use multiple tools on the same project for best results

cards.headline: Map Your Stack
cards.body: Sign up for free tiers of at least 2 tools: Runway (runway.ml) and one other (Pika, Kling, or Hailuo). Explore the interface for 5 minutes each. Note what feels intuitive.

quiz.question: Which AI video tool is best known for photorealistic, long-form generation?
quiz.explanation: Sora (by OpenAI) excels at photorealistic scenes with complex motion and can generate clips up to 60 seconds.

quiz.question: Runway Gen-3 is best known for its image-to-video pipeline.
quiz.explanation: Runway offers the best image-to-video workflow, allowing you to animate still images with precise motion control.

quiz.question: Which tool is recommended for stylised or animated content?
quiz.explanation: Pika excels at stylised, animated, or surreal content — making it ideal for creative and non-photorealistic work.

lessons.title: Prompting for Video
lessons.subtitle: How to write prompts that produce cinematic results

cards.headline: Your Script IS Your Camera
cards.body: In AI filmmaking, the prompt replaces the camera, the lighting rig, and the director's chair. A well-crafted prompt is the difference between amateur and cinematic.

cards.headline: The Anatomy of a Great Video Prompt
cards.body: Cinematic AI prompts follow a consistent structure: Subject + Action + Setting + Camera + Lighting + Style + Mood. Each element gives the AI more to work with.
bullets: Subject: Who or what is in frame
Action: What's happening (movement is key)
Setting: Where — time of day, environment
Camera: Shot type + movement (tracking, dolly, etc.)
Style: Film stock, colour grade, era
cards.statLabel: Quality improvement when using structured prompts vs simple descriptions

cards.headline: Prompt Examples: Before & After
cards.body: Weak prompt: "A woman walking in a city." Strong prompt: "A young woman in a camel trench coat walks through rain-slicked Tokyo streets at night. Neon signs reflect on wet pavement. Slow tracking shot from behind, shallow depth of field. Shot on 35mm Kodak Portra, Wong Kar-wai colour palette."
bullets: Specificity creates cinematic quality
Reference real film styles and directors
Include camera movement for dynamic results
Mention film stock for authentic grain and colour

cards.headline: Common Prompt Mistakes
cards.body: Most beginners over-describe or use contradictory instructions. The AI works best with clear, non-conflicting guidance.
bullets: Too vague: No visual anchor for the AI
Too long: Contradictions confuse generation
Static: Forgetting to include motion/action
Fix: Use prompt templates until it becomes instinct

cards.headline: Write 3 Cinematic Prompts
cards.body: Using the structure (Subject + Action + Setting + Camera + Style), write 3 prompts for scenes you'd love to see. Don't generate yet — just craft the language. We'll use these in Lesson 5.

quiz.question: What are the key elements of a structured video prompt?
options: Just describe what you want to see
Use as many words as possible
Copy the plot of a movie
quiz.explanation: A structured video prompt includes Subject, Action, Setting, Camera movement, and Style to give the AI clear cinematic direction.

quiz.question: Referencing real film styles or directors in prompts can improve output quality.
quiz.explanation: AI models trained on cinema understand references to directors and film stocks, producing more cohesive and stylised outputs.

quiz.question: What is the most common mistake in AI video prompts?
quiz.explanation: Prompts that are too vague give the AI no direction, while contradictory instructions confuse generation and produce inconsistent results.

lessons.title: Shot Types & Camera Language
lessons.subtitle: Cinematic grammar translated for AI video tools

cards.headline: Speak Like a Director
cards.body: Every great film uses deliberate shot choices. A close-up creates intimacy. A wide shot establishes scale. When you know this language, your AI outputs become truly cinematic.

cards.headline: Essential Shot Types
cards.body: Master these 6 core shot types and your AI films will feel professional instantly. Each communicates something different to the viewer.
bullets: Extreme Wide: Establishes world and scale
Wide/Full: Shows subject in environment
Medium: Conversational, natural framing
Close-Up: Emotion, detail, intimacy
Extreme Close-Up: Tension, micro-detail
Over-the-Shoulder: Connection between subjects
cards.statLabel: Core shot types that cover 90% of cinematic storytelling

cards.headline: Camera Movements That AI Understands
cards.body: AI video tools respond well to specific camera movement terminology. Using the right words transforms static clips into dynamic cinema.
bullets: Dolly in/out: Camera physically moves toward/away
Tracking shot: Camera follows alongside subject
Crane/aerial: Rising or descending movement
Pan/tilt: Camera rotates on its axis
Steadicam: Smooth handheld following movement
Whip pan: Fast rotational movement for energy

cards.headline: Combining Shots & Movement
cards.body: The magic happens when you combine shot type with movement. "Slow dolly in to close-up" creates building tension. "Aerial tracking wide shot" establishes epic scale. Think in combinations.
bullets: Dolly + Close-up = building intensity
Tracking + Medium = following action
Crane + Wide = establishing grandeur
Tip: Add speed (slow, fast) for mood control

cards.headline: Translate a Scene
cards.body: Think of a favourite movie scene. Break it into 3-4 shots using proper terminology (e.g., "Slow tracking medium shot of character walking through rain"). This is how you'll direct your AI.

quiz.question: Which shot type is best for conveying emotion and intimacy?
quiz.explanation: Close-ups focus on facial expressions and fine detail, creating emotional connection and intimacy with the viewer.

quiz.question: A "dolly in" means the camera physically moves toward the subject.
quiz.explanation: A dolly movement means the camera itself moves through space (toward or away from the subject), unlike a zoom which just changes focal length.

quiz.question: What combination of shot type and movement creates a sense of epic scale?
quiz.explanation: Combining a wide shot with crane or aerial movement reveals the full scope of an environment, creating a feeling of grandeur and epic scale.

lessons.title: Your First AI Scene
lessons.subtitle: Create a 10-second cinematic clip from scratch

cards.headline: From Words to Moving Pictures
cards.body: Everything you've learned so far converges here. Today you generate your first real cinematic clip — and feel the rush of seeing your vision come to life.

cards.headline: The Generation Workflow
cards.body: Professional AI filmmakers don't just type one prompt and hope. They follow a systematic workflow that maximises quality while minimising wasted credits.
bullets: Step 1: Write your structured prompt (Lesson 3 format)
Step 2: Generate 3-4 variations at low resolution
Step 3: Evaluate — pick the best motion and composition
Step 4: Regenerate the winner at full quality
Step 5: Download and review frame-by-frame
cards.statLabel: Variations you should generate before committing to final quality

cards.headline: Iteration is Everything
cards.body: Your first generation will rarely be perfect. The skill isn't in getting it right first time — it's in reading the output and refining your prompt intelligently.
bullets: Too static? Add action verbs and camera movement
Wrong mood? Adjust lighting and colour references
Weird artifacts? Simplify the prompt, remove conflicts
Good but not great? Add a film stock or director reference

cards.headline: Quality Checkpoints
cards.body: Before you call a clip "done," run it through these quality checks. This separates amateur AI clips from professional output.
bullets: Motion: Is movement smooth and natural?
Consistency: Do elements maintain shape throughout?
Composition: Is framing visually balanced?
Mood: Does the lighting/colour match your intent?

cards.headline: Generate Your Scene
cards.body: Take your best prompt from Lesson 3. Open Runway or your chosen tool. Generate 3 variations. Pick the best one. Then refine the prompt and generate again. Save your final clip — this is Day 1 of your portfolio.

quiz.question: What is the recommended first step in the AI video generation workflow?
options: Write a structured prompt using the format from Lesson 3
Copy a prompt from the internet
Start with the longest possible clip
quiz.explanation: Always start with a carefully structured prompt before generating. This maximises your chances of a good result and minimises wasted credits.

quiz.question: You should generate multiple variations before committing to final quality.
quiz.explanation: Generating 3-4 variations at lower resolution lets you find the best composition and motion before spending credits on full-quality output.

quiz.question: If your AI clip feels too static, what should you adjust?
options: Add action verbs and camera movement
quiz.explanation: Static clips usually mean the prompt lacks motion. Adding action verbs and camera movement terminology gives the AI clear dynamic direction.

lessons.title: Story Structure for Short Films
lessons.subtitle: 3-act structure compressed to 60–180 seconds

cards.headline: Even 60 Seconds Needs a Story
cards.body: A beautiful clip without narrative is wallpaper. A structured story — even at 60 seconds — creates emotion, retention, and shareability.

cards.headline: The Micro 3-Act Structure
cards.body: Every story — from a 2-hour film to a 60-second short — follows the same emotional arc. For AI short films, we compress it radically.
bullets: Act 1 (0-15s): Hook + World Setup — establish character and world instantly
Act 2 (15-45s): Tension + Journey — introduce a challenge or transformation
Act 3 (45-60s): Resolution + Emotion — deliver the payoff or twist
Total: 3-5 scenes that flow into each other
cards.statLabel: Scenes needed for a compelling 60-second AI short film

cards.headline: Emotional Beats, Not Plot Points
cards.body: In short-form video, you don't have time for complex plot. Instead, focus on emotional beats — moments that make the viewer feel something.
bullets: Wonder: Show something visually extraordinary
Tension: Create anticipation or uncertainty
Surprise: Subvert expectations
Resolution: Deliver satisfaction or catharsis
Tip: One strong emotion > three weak ones

cards.headline: Short Film Archetypes That Work
cards.body: Certain story patterns perform exceptionally well in AI short films because they're visually driven and emotionally simple.
bullets: The Journey: Character travels through changing worlds
The Transformation: Something evolves or morphs
The Reveal: Build to a surprising visual payoff
The Loop: Ending connects back to the beginning
The Contrast: Two opposing visuals juxtaposed

cards.headline: Plan Your First Short
cards.body: Choose one archetype (Journey, Transformation, Reveal, Loop, or Contrast). Write 3-5 scene descriptions of 1-2 sentences each. This is your story skeleton — we'll build the full script next.

quiz.question: How long should Act 1 (Hook + World Setup) be in a 60-second short film?
quiz.explanation: In a micro 3-act structure, Act 1 should be 0-15 seconds — just enough to hook the viewer and establish the world before tension begins.

quiz.question: Short-form AI films should focus on emotional beats rather than complex plot.
quiz.explanation: With limited time, emotional moments are more impactful than intricate plot details. One strong feeling beats multiple weak story points.

quiz.question: Which short film archetype involves building to a surprising visual payoff?
quiz.explanation: The Reveal archetype builds anticipation throughout the film, then delivers a surprising visual payoff that recontextualises everything before it.

lessons.title: Scriptwriting with AI
lessons.subtitle: Use Claude/ChatGPT to write screenplays and shot lists

cards.headline: Your AI Writing Partner
cards.body: The best AI filmmakers don't just use AI for video generation — they use it to write scripts, create shot lists, and plan entire productions in minutes.

cards.headline: The AI Scriptwriting Workflow
cards.body: Use Claude or ChatGPT as your writing room. Start with your story skeleton and expand it into a proper micro-screenplay with visual direction.
bullets: Step 1: Feed your story archetype and scene descriptions
Step 2: Ask for a shot-by-shot breakdown
Step 3: Request video generation prompts for each shot
Step 4: Add timing and pacing notes
Step 5: Review and refine for visual coherence
cards.statLabel: Time to generate a complete short film script with AI assistance

cards.headline: The Perfect Shot List Format
cards.body: A shot list bridges your script and your AI video tool. Each entry should translate directly into a generation prompt.
bullets: Shot #: Sequential numbering
Duration: How long this clip runs (3-10s)
Visual: Detailed description of what's on screen
Camera: Shot type + movement
Mood/Style: Lighting, colour, film reference
Audio: What sound accompanies this shot

cards.headline: Prompt Engineering for Scripts
cards.body: The key to great AI scripts is giving the LLM the right context. Treat it like briefing a screenwriter.
bullets: Specify genre, mood, and target audience
Give examples of films or videos you admire
Ask for "visually-driven" scenes — minimal dialogue
Request that each shot be "self-contained" for AI generation
Iterate: Ask for alternatives if the first draft feels generic

cards.headline: Generate Your Shot List
cards.body: Take your story skeleton from Lesson 6. Paste it into Claude or ChatGPT with this instruction: "Turn this into a 5-shot cinematic short film. For each shot, give me: duration, visual description, camera movement, mood, and a detailed video generation prompt." Save the output.

quiz.question: What should each entry in a shot list include?
options: Shot number, duration, visual, camera, mood, and audio
quiz.explanation: A complete shot list entry includes shot number, duration, visual description, camera movement, mood/style, and audio — providing everything needed for generation.

quiz.question: AI-written scripts for short films should be visually driven with minimal dialogue.
quiz.explanation: Since AI video tools generate visuals (not speech), scripts should focus on what's seen rather than what's said. Visual storytelling is the priority.

quiz.question: What is the recommended approach if the first AI-generated script feels generic?
options: Start over with a different tool
Iterate — ask for alternatives and refine
quiz.explanation: Iteration is key. Ask the AI for alternatives, provide more specific references, or request different tones until the script feels unique and compelling.

lessons.title: Visual Storyboarding
lessons.subtitle: Generate storyboard frames with AI image tools

cards.headline: See Before You Shoot
cards.body: Hollywood directors storyboard every shot before cameras roll. AI lets you create photorealistic storyboards in minutes — giving you a visual blueprint before spending a single video credit.

cards.headline: Why Storyboard First
cards.body: Generating video is expensive (credits) and time-consuming. A storyboard lets you lock in composition, style, and pacing before committing to video generation.
bullets: Save 60-80% on video credits by pre-visualising
Catch continuity issues before they're baked in
Experiment with framing and colour freely
Share with clients for approval before production
Use as direct reference images for image-to-video
cards.statLabel: Credit savings when storyboarding before video generation

cards.headline: AI Storyboarding Workflow
cards.body: Use Midjourney, DALL-E, or Flux to generate each frame of your shot list as a still image. Then these stills become your image-to-video inputs.
bullets: Convert each shot list entry into an image prompt
Add "--ar 16:9" for cinematic aspect ratio
Keep style consistent: same colour palette, lighting
Generate 2-3 options per shot, pick the strongest
Arrange in sequence to check visual flow

cards.headline: From Storyboard to Video
cards.body: The real power move: use your storyboard frames as direct inputs for image-to-video tools like Runway. This gives you far more control over the final output than text-to-video alone.
bullets: Upload storyboard frame → Runway image-to-video
Add motion instructions: "camera dollies forward slowly"
Result: Your exact composition, now in motion
Consistency: Same subject appearance across all shots
Tip: Keep image simple — complex frames generate messier video

cards.headline: Create Your Storyboard
cards.body: Take your shot list from Lesson 7. Generate one AI image per shot using Midjourney, DALL-E, or Flux (free tiers work). Arrange them in order. You now have a visual storyboard for your short film.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of storyboarding before video generation?
options: It saves credits by pre-visualising shots
It replaces the need for prompts
quiz.explanation: Storyboarding lets you lock in composition and style with cheap image generation before spending expensive video credits on final clips.

quiz.question: Storyboard images can be used as direct inputs for image-to-video tools like Runway.
quiz.explanation: Image-to-video pipelines accept your storyboard frame and animate it, giving you precise control over the starting composition of each shot.

quiz.question: What aspect ratio should you use for cinematic storyboard frames?
quiz.explanation: 16:9 is the standard cinematic widescreen ratio used in film and YouTube — it ensures your storyboards match your final video format.

lessons.title: Continuity & Character Consistency
lessons.subtitle: Keeping subjects consistent across scenes

cards.headline: The Biggest AI Video Challenge
cards.body: Your character looks different in every shot. Their hair changes, their clothes shift, their face morphs. This is the #1 problem in AI filmmaking — and there are proven solutions.

cards.headline: Why Consistency Is Hard
cards.body: AI video models generate each clip independently. They have no "memory" of previous shots. Without deliberate techniques, every generation creates a slightly different version of your subject.
bullets: Each generation is statistically independent
Small prompt variations cause visual drift
Faces are especially prone to inconsistency
Clothing, lighting, and environment all shift
This is why multi-shot films look amateur without techniques

cards.headline: Technique 1: Reference Image Anchoring
cards.body: The most reliable method: create one definitive reference image of your character and use it as the input for every shot.
bullets: Generate a "character sheet" with multiple angles
Use image-to-video for every shot (never pure text-to-video)
Keep the same seed/style settings across generations
Kling and Runway both support character reference uploads
Tip: Simple, distinctive character designs stay more consistent
cards.statLabel: Consistency improvement when using reference images vs text-only

cards.headline: Technique 2: Prompt Anchoring & Style Lock
cards.body: When reference images aren't possible, use identical descriptive phrases across all prompts to maintain visual consistency.
bullets: Create a "character block" — exact same description in every prompt
Lock style references: same film stock, director, era in all shots
Use identical lighting descriptions throughout
Keep environment elements consistent (time of day, weather)
Copy-paste your character block — don't retype it each time

cards.headline: Build Your Character Sheet
cards.body: Design a character for your short film. Generate 3-4 images of them in different poses/angles using the same prompt structure. Save the best as your "reference sheet." This anchors all future shots.

quiz.question: Why do AI-generated characters look different across shots?
options: Each generation is independent with no memory of previous shots
quiz.explanation: AI models generate each clip independently — they have no memory or awareness of previous outputs, causing visual drift between shots.

quiz.question: Using a reference image for every shot improves character consistency by approximately 85%.
quiz.explanation: Reference image anchoring is the most reliable consistency technique, providing the AI with a visual anchor rather than relying on text descriptions alone.

quiz.question: What is a "character block" in AI filmmaking?
options: An exact copy-pasted description used in every prompt
A video clip of the character
quiz.explanation: A character block is the same descriptive text pasted into every prompt — ensuring the AI receives identical character instructions for each shot.

lessons.title: Sound Design & AI Music
lessons.subtitle: AI-generated soundtracks, SFX, and voiceover

cards.headline: Sound Makes the Film
cards.body: Remove the audio from any film and it feels flat, lifeless. Sound is 50% of the cinematic experience — and AI can now generate professional soundtracks, sound effects, and voiceover on demand.

cards.headline: The Audio Stack for AI Films
cards.body: A professional AI film has three audio layers that work together. Each can now be generated or sourced with AI tools.
bullets: Layer 1: Music — Sets emotional tone and pacing
Layer 2: Sound Effects (SFX) — Adds realism and texture
Layer 3: Voiceover/Dialogue — Narrates or communicates
Mixing: Balance all three so nothing fights for attention
Rule: Music at 60%, SFX at 80%, VO at 100% volume as starting point
cards.statLabel: Of the cinematic experience comes from audio, not visuals

cards.headline: AI Music Generation
cards.body: Tools like Suno, Udio, and Stable Audio generate broadcast-quality music from text descriptions. You can match the exact mood, tempo, and genre of your film.
bullets: Suno: Best for full songs with vocals and lyrics
Udio: Superior audio quality, great instrumentals
Stable Audio: Precise duration control, stems output
Tip: Specify BPM, genre, mood, and instruments
Commercial rights: Check each tool's license for client work

cards.headline: AI Voiceover & Sound Effects
cards.body: ElevenLabs leads AI voiceover with natural-sounding narration in any tone. For SFX, tools like ElevenLabs Sound Effects and Freesound cover everything.
bullets: ElevenLabs: Ultra-realistic narration in 30+ languages
Voice cloning: Create a consistent narrator voice
AI SFX: Describe the sound you need in text
Ambient layers: Rain, traffic, wind — generate or source freely
Tip: Layer 2-3 subtle ambient sounds for cinematic depth

cards.headline: Score Your Film
cards.body: Open Suno or Udio (free tiers available). Describe the mood of your short film and generate a 30-60 second instrumental track. Then find or generate 2-3 sound effects that match your scenes. Save these for assembly in Lesson 11.

quiz.question: What are the three audio layers in a professional AI film?
quiz.explanation: The three layers are music (emotional tone), sound effects (realism and texture), and voiceover/dialogue (narration). Balanced together they create cinematic audio.

quiz.question: Suno and Udio can generate broadcast-quality music from text descriptions.
quiz.explanation: Both Suno and Udio generate professional-quality music from text prompts describing genre, mood, tempo, and instrumentation.

quiz.question: Which tool leads in AI voiceover with ultra-realistic narration?
quiz.explanation: ElevenLabs is the leading AI voiceover tool, offering natural-sounding narration in 30+ languages with voice cloning capabilities.

lessons.title: Editing Your AI Film
lessons.subtitle: Assembling cuts, pacing, and transitions

cards.headline: The Edit Is Where Films Are Made
cards.body: You have clips, music, and sound effects. Now comes the craft that transforms raw footage into a story — editing. This is where amateur content becomes cinematic.

cards.headline: Your Editing Toolkit
cards.body: You don't need expensive software. Free and affordable tools handle AI film editing perfectly.
bullets: CapCut (Free): Best for short-form, mobile-friendly editing
DaVinci Resolve (Free): Professional-grade, colour grading included
Adobe Premiere Pro: Industry standard, subscription-based
Descript: AI-powered editing with transcript-based cuts
For beginners: Start with CapCut — it's the fastest path to results

cards.headline: Pacing & Rhythm
cards.body: Great editing is about rhythm. Each cut should feel intentional — driven by the music beat, an emotional shift, or a narrative transition.
bullets: Cut on the beat: Align scene changes to music hits
Hold shots longer for tension, cut faster for energy
3-second rule: Most shots work best at 3-5 seconds
Let key moments breathe — don't rush your best visuals
Match pacing to emotion: slow = reflective, fast = exciting
cards.statLabel: Optimal shot duration for most AI short film scenes

cards.headline: Transitions That Work
cards.body: Forget star wipes and spinning transitions. Cinematic films use simple, intentional transitions that serve the story.
bullets: Hard cut: Default for most scene changes (clean, professional)
Cross-dissolve: Time passing or emotional shift
Match cut: Visual similarity bridges two different scenes
Fade to black: Chapter ending, major time skip
Rule: If a transition draws attention to itself, it's wrong

cards.headline: Assemble Your Film
cards.body: Import your generated clips into CapCut or DaVinci Resolve. Arrange them in story order. Add your AI music track underneath. Cut clips to the beat. Add 1-2 cross-dissolves where scenes shift emotionally. Export at 1080p.

quiz.question: Which free editing tool is recommended for beginners making AI short films?
quiz.explanation: CapCut is free, intuitive, and the fastest path to results for beginners. It handles short-form content editing perfectly.

quiz.question: Most shots in an AI short film work best at 3-5 seconds duration.
quiz.explanation: The 3-5 second sweet spot gives viewers enough time to absorb the visual without losing momentum in the edit.

quiz.question: What is the default transition type for professional cinematic editing?
quiz.explanation: Hard cuts are the default in professional filmmaking — they're clean, invisible, and let the content speak without distraction.

lessons.title: Brand Video Fundamentals
lessons.subtitle: What makes a brand video convert

cards.headline: Brands Pay Premium for Video
cards.body: A single 60-second brand video can cost £5,000-£50,000 from a traditional agency. With AI, you can deliver the same impact at a fraction of the cost — and businesses are desperate for this.

cards.headline: What Brand Video Actually Is
cards.body: Brand video isn't just "a video about a brand." It's strategic visual storytelling designed to achieve a specific business outcome.
bullets: Awareness: Make people know you exist (top of funnel)
Consideration: Show why you're the right choice (mid funnel)
Conversion: Drive immediate action (bottom of funnel)
Retention: Keep customers engaged and loyal
Each type has different length, style, and call-to-action
cards.statLabel: Traditional agency cost for a single 60-second brand video

cards.headline: The Anatomy of High-Converting Brand Video
cards.body: Videos that drive results follow a proven formula. Every second earns the next second of attention.
bullets: Hook (0-3s): Pattern interrupt — stop the scroll instantly
Problem (3-10s): Articulate their pain clearly
Solution (10-25s): Show the transformation your brand enables
Proof (25-40s): Evidence — results, testimonials, demo
CTA (40-60s): Clear, single action to take next

cards.headline: AI Brand Video Advantages
cards.body: AI video creation has specific advantages for brand content that traditional production can't match.
bullets: Speed: Deliver in days, not weeks
Iteration: Test 10 versions for the cost of 1 traditional
Consistency: Same style across all content effortlessly
Scale: Produce for every platform simultaneously
Personalisation: Localise for different markets easily

cards.headline: Deconstruct a Brand Video
cards.body: Find a brand video ad on YouTube or social media (Nike, Apple, or any brand you admire). Map its structure: Hook → Problem → Solution → Proof → CTA. Note the timing of each section. This pattern becomes your template.

quiz.question: What should the first 3 seconds of a brand video accomplish?
quiz.explanation: The first 3 seconds must hook attention with a pattern interrupt. If you don't stop the scroll, nothing else matters.

quiz.question: AI brand videos can be produced in days rather than the weeks required by traditional agencies.
quiz.explanation: AI video tools dramatically compress production timelines — what takes traditional agencies weeks of filming and editing can be done in days with AI.

quiz.question: What is the correct structure for a high-converting brand video?
quiz.explanation: The proven structure is Hook (stop attention), Problem (pain), Solution (transformation), Proof (evidence), CTA (action) — each second earning the next.

lessons.title: Product Videos with AI
lessons.subtitle: Showcase products without a studio

cards.headline: Studio-Quality Product Shots, Zero Studio
cards.body: Product photography studios charge £500+ per day. AI can generate photorealistic product scenes, dynamic reveals, and lifestyle shots — all from a single product photo.

cards.headline: AI Product Video Types
cards.body: Different products need different video treatments. Know which type works for your client's product category.
bullets: Hero Reveal: Dramatic entrance, cinematic lighting
Lifestyle Context: Product in use, real-world setting
360° Showcase: Rotating view showing all angles
Feature Highlight: Zoom into specific details
Before/After: Transformation the product enables
cards.statLabel: Of shoppers are more likely to buy after watching a product video

cards.headline: The Product Video Workflow
cards.body: A systematic process for turning any product photo into a dynamic, selling video.
bullets: Step 1: Get the best product photo (clean background, high-res)
Step 2: Use AI to place product in aspirational environments
Step 3: Generate image-to-video with slow, elegant motion
Step 4: Add subtle SFX (whoosh, ambient, surface texture)
Step 5: Overlay text with key feature or price point

cards.headline: Prompting for Product Videos
cards.body: Product videos need specific prompt language to achieve that premium, commercial feel.
bullets: Use: "product photography, studio lighting, premium feel"
Movement: "slow 360 rotation" or "gentle dolly in"
Environment: "marble surface," "soft gradient background"
Lighting: "rim light, soft key light, no harsh shadows"
Avoid: Fast camera moves, complex backgrounds, multiple products

cards.headline: Create a Product Video
cards.body: Pick any product (something on your desk, a favourite brand). Take or find a clean photo of it. Use AI to generate it in 2-3 different environments. Then use image-to-video to add gentle motion. You now have a product showcase reel.

quiz.question: What percentage of shoppers are more likely to buy after watching a product video?
quiz.explanation: 73% of shoppers say product video makes them more likely to purchase — making it one of the highest-ROI content types for e-commerce.

quiz.question: The best product videos typically use fast camera movements for energy.
quiz.explanation: Product videos work best with slow, elegant motion — gentle dolly-ins, slow rotations. Fast movement looks chaotic and distracts from the product itself.

quiz.question: What is the first step in the AI product video workflow?
options: Get a high-quality product photo with clean background
quiz.explanation: Everything starts with a great product photo — clean background, high resolution. This becomes the input for AI environment placement and video generation.

lessons.title: Testimonial & Social Proof Videos
lessons.subtitle: AI-enhanced customer story videos

cards.headline: Nothing Sells Like Social Proof
cards.body: People trust other people more than brands. Testimonial videos convert at 2× the rate of feature videos — and AI lets you produce them at scale without flying a film crew to every customer.

cards.headline: AI-Enhanced Testimonial Formats
cards.body: You don't need to replace real customer voices — you enhance them. AI handles the production quality that makes amateur testimonials look professional.
bullets: Text-to-video: Animate customer quotes into visual stories
Audio enhancement: Clean up phone-recorded testimonials
B-roll generation: Create relevant visuals to cover jump cuts
Subtitle styling: Professional animated captions
Compilation: Edit 10 short clips into one powerful montage
cards.statLabel: Conversion rate improvement of testimonial videos vs feature videos

cards.headline: The Customer Story Framework
cards.body: Every great testimonial follows a narrative arc. Coach your client's customers to share their story in this structure.
bullets: Before: What was life/business like before? (the pain)
Decision: What made them choose this product/service?
Experience: What was the implementation like?
After: What's different now? (specific results)
Recommend: Would they recommend it? Why?

cards.headline: Production Techniques
cards.body: Practical techniques to produce professional testimonial videos using AI tools.
bullets: Get audio via voice memo — no filming needed
Generate B-roll that illustrates their story (AI video)
Use AI voiceover if customer is camera-shy (with permission)
Add kinetic text for key stats and quotes
Background music: Subtle, uplifting, never overpowering

cards.headline: Build a Testimonial Template
cards.body: Create a 30-second testimonial video template: Find or write a sample customer quote. Generate 3-4 AI B-roll clips that illustrate the transformation. Add subtle music, animated text of the quote, and a CTA at the end. This template works for any client.

quiz.question: How much more effective are testimonial videos compared to feature videos for conversion?
quiz.explanation: Testimonial videos convert at twice the rate of feature-focused videos because people trust other customers more than brand claims.

quiz.question: AI testimonial videos should completely replace real customer voices with AI-generated ones.
quiz.explanation: AI should enhance real customer testimonials (clean audio, add B-roll, style subtitles) — not replace authentic voices. Authenticity is what makes testimonials powerful.

quiz.question: What is the correct narrative arc for a customer testimonial?
quiz.explanation: The Before → Decision → Experience → After → Recommend framework captures the full customer journey and creates an emotionally compelling story.

lessons.title: YouTube Content Machine
lessons.subtitle: Faceless YouTube channels powered by AI

cards.headline: Faceless Channels Are Printing Money
cards.body: Thousands of YouTube channels earn £5K-£50K/month without ever showing a face. They use AI for scripts, visuals, voiceover, and editing. You now have every skill to build one.

cards.headline: Faceless YouTube Niches That Work
cards.body: Not all niches work for AI-generated faceless content. The best ones are visually rich, evergreen, and have high CPM (ad revenue per view).
bullets: Luxury/Travel: AI cinematic footage of destinations
History/Documentaries: AI-generated historical visuals
Science/Space: Cosmic and microscopic AI visuals
Motivation/Self-Improvement: Visual metaphors + AI VO
Finance/Business: Clean graphics + AI narration
cards.statLabel: CPM range for high-value faceless YouTube niches

cards.headline: The AI YouTube Production Pipeline
cards.body: A streamlined workflow that lets you publish 3-5 videos per week — entirely AI-powered.
bullets: Step 1: Use ChatGPT/Claude to research trending topics
Step 2: Generate a 5-8 minute script with hook + retention loops
Step 3: Create AI voiceover with ElevenLabs
Step 4: Generate AI B-roll for every scene (Runway/Kling)
Step 5: Edit in CapCut, add captions, export
Step 6: Optimise title + thumbnail with AI assistance

cards.headline: Retention & Algorithm Secrets
cards.body: YouTube rewards watch time above all else. Your AI content must be engineered to keep viewers watching.
bullets: Pattern interrupt every 30 seconds (new visual, sound, energy shift)
Open loops: Tease what's coming to prevent clicks away
First 30 seconds = most critical (hook or lose them)
Vary shot types: Wide → Close → Motion → Text overlay
End with a strong CTA to watch another video (session time)

cards.headline: Plan Your Channel
cards.body: Choose a niche from the list above. Use AI to generate 10 video title ideas with high click potential. Pick your best 3. Write a script outline for video #1 using the retention principles. This is your channel blueprint.

quiz.question: What is the most important metric YouTube uses to recommend videos?
quiz.explanation: YouTube's algorithm prioritises watch time and retention above all other metrics. Videos that keep viewers watching get recommended more.

quiz.question: Faceless YouTube channels can earn £5K-£50K per month using AI-generated content.
quiz.explanation: Thousands of faceless channels in high-CPM niches earn significant revenue using AI for scripts, visuals, voiceover, and editing.

quiz.question: How often should you use "pattern interrupts" in YouTube content?
quiz.explanation: Pattern interrupts every 30 seconds (new visual, sound change, energy shift) keep viewers engaged and prevent them from clicking away.

lessons.title: Short-Form Viral Content
lessons.subtitle: TikTok, Reels, and Shorts with AI

cards.headline: One Viral Clip Can Change Everything
cards.body: A single 15-60 second AI video can reach millions organically. Short-form is the fastest path to audience, clients, and revenue — and AI gives you an unfair production advantage.

cards.headline: Platform-Specific Formats
cards.body: Each platform has subtle differences in what performs. Optimise your AI content for where it will live.
bullets: TikTok: Raw energy, trend-riding, text overlays, fast cuts
Instagram Reels: Polished aesthetic, aspirational, smooth transitions
YouTube Shorts: Educational hooks, "Did you know?" format
All platforms: 9:16 vertical, captions mandatory, hook in 1 second
Tip: Repurpose one concept into 3 platform-native versions
cards.statLabel: Time you have to hook a viewer on short-form before they swipe

cards.headline: AI Short-Form Video Formulas
cards.body: Proven content formulas that work exceptionally well with AI-generated visuals.
bullets: Satisfying loops: Mesmerising visuals that auto-replay
Mini-documentaries: 60-second stories with cinematic AI footage
Before/After: Transformations powered by AI visuals
Explainers: Complex topics made visual with AI
"POV" content: First-person perspective AI scenes
Trend mashups: Current audio trends + AI-generated visuals

cards.headline: The Viral Checklist
cards.body: Before posting any AI short-form content, run it through this quality gate.
bullets: Hook test: Would YOU stop scrolling for this in 1 second?
Loop test: Does the ending connect to the beginning?
Sound test: Does it work both with and without audio?
Share test: Would someone tag a friend in the comments?
Replay test: Is there a reason to watch it twice?

cards.headline: Create a Viral-Ready Short
cards.body: Pick one formula (satisfying loop, mini-doc, or before/after). Generate 3-5 AI clips in 9:16 vertical format. Edit them into a 15-30 second piece with trending audio or AI music. Add captions. Post it to your chosen platform.

quiz.question: What aspect ratio should all short-form content use?
quiz.explanation: 9:16 vertical is the standard for all short-form platforms (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) — it fills the full mobile screen.

quiz.question: Captions are optional on short-form video content.
quiz.explanation: Captions are mandatory — most viewers watch without sound initially, and captions significantly increase watch time and accessibility.

quiz.question: Which short-form formula involves mesmerising visuals that encourage auto-replay?
quiz.explanation: Satisfying loops create mesmerising visuals where the ending connects seamlessly back to the beginning, encouraging viewers to watch multiple times.

lessons.title: Building Your Video Portfolio
lessons.subtitle: Showreel structure and presentation

cards.headline: Your Portfolio Is Your Proof
cards.body: No one cares about your tools or process. Clients buy results. A killer portfolio — even with 100% AI-generated work — lands you £2,500+ projects when it looks professional.

cards.headline: Portfolio Structure
cards.body: Organise your portfolio to make the buying decision easy. Clients should see your best work within 10 seconds and understand what you offer within 30.
bullets: Showreel (30-60s): Your absolute best clips, fast-paced montage
Category sections: Brand, Product, Short Film, Social
Case studies: 2-3 projects with context (brief, process, result)
About: Short bio positioning you as an AI video specialist
CTA: Clear way to hire you or book a call
cards.statLabel: Time a potential client spends before deciding to explore further

cards.headline: The Perfect Showreel
cards.body: Your showreel is your most important asset. It should be a high-energy highlight reel of your absolute best work.
bullets: Length: 30-60 seconds maximum (shorter = more impact)
Open with your single strongest shot (the hook)
Cut to the beat — music drives the pacing
Variety: Show range (different styles, subjects, moods)
End with a title card: your name + contact
Update monthly: Replace weakest clip with newest best

cards.headline: Where to Host
cards.body: Your portfolio needs to live where clients can find it and be impressed.
bullets: Personal website: Squarespace, Framer, or custom build
Vimeo: Professional video hosting, better than YouTube for portfolios
Instagram grid: Curated feed of your best clips
Behance: Creative community, good for discovery
Tip: Link everything to one central portfolio page

cards.headline: Build Your Showreel
cards.body: Gather your 5-8 best AI clips from this course. Edit them into a 30-second showreel cut to music. Focus on variety and impact. Upload to Vimeo or your website. This is now your calling card.

quiz.question: How long should a video portfolio showreel be?
quiz.explanation: 30-60 seconds is the sweet spot — long enough to show range, short enough to hold attention. Shorter reels are more impactful than longer ones.

quiz.question: You should update your showreel monthly by replacing your weakest clip with your newest best work.
quiz.explanation: Regular updates ensure your showreel always represents your current skill level. As you improve, old work should be cycled out.

quiz.question: What should you open your showreel with?
quiz.explanation: Lead with your absolute best shot — it hooks viewers immediately and sets the quality expectation for everything that follows.

lessons.title: Freelance AI Video Services
lessons.subtitle: Pricing and packaging video production

cards.headline: Get Paid to Create
cards.body: Businesses need video yesterday. They don't care if it's AI or traditional — they care about speed, quality, and results. Position yourself correctly and you'll never struggle to find clients.

cards.headline: Service Packages That Sell
cards.body: Don't sell "AI video." Sell outcomes. Package your services into clear tiers that match different budgets and needs.
bullets: Starter (£500-£1,000): 3-5 short-form videos, basic editing
Growth (£1,500-£3,000): Brand video + 10 social clips + music
Premium (£3,000-£7,500): Full campaign: hero video, social suite, ads
Retainer (£1,500-£3,000/mo): Ongoing content: 10-20 videos/month
Tip: Always include a revision round in your pricing
cards.statLabel: Average project value for AI video freelancers with strong portfolios

cards.headline: Finding Your First Clients
cards.body: You don't need a massive following. You need 3-5 paying clients to build momentum and case studies.
bullets: Local businesses: Restaurants, gyms, salons — they need video but can't afford agencies
E-commerce brands: Product videos for every SKU
Coaches/consultants: Personal brand content
Real estate: Property showcase videos
Cold outreach: Show them what their content COULD look like with AI

cards.headline: The Irresistible Pitch
cards.body: Your pitch should make it impossible for a business owner to say no.
bullets: Lead with a free sample: Create a 15-second clip of THEIR brand
Compare: Show the £5K+ agency quote vs your pricing
Speed: Promise delivery in 3-5 days, not 3-5 weeks
Show ROI: "This video style increased conversions 40% for Brand X"
Remove risk: Offer money-back if they're not satisfied

cards.headline: Create Your Service Menu
cards.body: Write out your 3 service tiers with pricing, deliverables, and turnaround time. Then pick one local business and create a free 15-second sample video using their branding (colours, logo). Send it to them with your pitch.

quiz.question: What is the recommended approach to pitching AI video services?
options: Send a long email about AI technology
Lead with a free sample of THEIR brand
quiz.explanation: Leading with a free sample tailored to their brand makes the value immediately tangible. It's nearly impossible to ignore seeing your own brand in a professional video.

quiz.question: You should sell "AI video" services rather than outcomes and results.
quiz.explanation: Clients don't care about the tools — they care about speed, quality, and results. Sell the outcome (conversions, content, brand presence), not the technology.

quiz.question: What is the typical delivery turnaround for AI video services compared to traditional agencies?
quiz.explanation: AI video can be delivered in 3-5 days compared to 3-5 weeks for traditional agencies — this speed is a major competitive advantage.

lessons.title: Selling Stock AI Footage
lessons.subtitle: Passive income from AI-generated clips

cards.headline: Earn While You Sleep
cards.body: Every AI clip you create can be sold thousands of times on stock platforms. Build a library once, earn passive income forever. Some AI creators make £3,000+/month from stock footage alone.

cards.headline: Stock Footage Platforms
cards.body: Multiple platforms accept AI-generated footage. Each has different audiences, pricing, and requirements.
bullets: Shutterstock: Largest marketplace, accepts AI content (labelled)
Adobe Stock: Integrated into Creative Cloud, high demand
Pond5: Premium pricing, creative/artistic clips sell well
Artgrid: Subscription model, cinematic focus
Tip: Upload to 2-3 platforms simultaneously for maximum reach
cards.statLabel: Monthly passive income achievable with a library of 500+ quality clips

cards.headline: What Sells on Stock Platforms
cards.body: Not all footage sells equally. Understand market demand to create clips that generate consistent revenue.
bullets: Business/corporate: Office scenes, teamwork, technology
Nature/aerial: Landscapes, weather, water, seasons
Abstract/motion: Particles, gradients, textures, loops
Lifestyle: Wellness, fitness, cooking, travel
Trending: AI/tech visuals, sustainability, remote work

cards.headline: Optimising for Sales
cards.body: Upload quality and metadata determine whether your clips get found and purchased.
bullets: Resolution: Always upload 4K when possible
Duration: 10-30 seconds is the sweet spot
Keywords: Use 20-30 relevant, specific tags per clip
Titles: Descriptive, keyword-rich titles
Collections: Group related clips for bundle purchases
Volume: Aim for 50+ clips/month to build momentum

cards.headline: Upload Your First 5 Clips
cards.body: Generate 5 high-quality stock clips in a popular category (abstract, nature, or business). Ensure 4K resolution, 10-20 seconds each. Write keyword-rich titles and 25+ tags. Upload to Shutterstock or Adobe Stock. Track your first sales.

quiz.question: Which stock platform is the largest marketplace for video footage?
quiz.explanation: Shutterstock is the world's largest stock marketplace with the highest volume of buyers. They accept AI-generated content when properly labelled.

quiz.question: Stock footage clips should ideally be 10-30 seconds long for best sales.
quiz.explanation: 10-30 seconds is the sweet spot for stock footage — long enough to be useful in edits, short enough to fit various project needs.

quiz.question: How many clips per month should you aim to upload to build momentum?
quiz.explanation: Aim for 50+ clips per month to build a library quickly. Volume is key to passive income — more clips means more chances of being found and purchased.

lessons.title: AI Video for Clients
lessons.subtitle: Managing projects, revisions, and delivery

cards.headline: Professional Delivery = Repeat Clients
cards.body: Great video is only half the job. How you manage the project — communication, process, delivery — determines whether a one-off becomes a retainer client.

cards.headline: The Client Project Workflow
cards.body: A structured process makes you look professional, sets expectations, and prevents scope creep.
bullets: 1. Discovery call: Understand goals, audience, brand guidelines
2. Creative brief: Document everything in writing
3. Storyboard/concept: Visual mockup for approval before production
4. First draft: Deliver rough cut for feedback
5. Revisions: 1-2 rounds included in pricing
6. Final delivery: Multiple formats for all platforms
cards.statLabel: Of client issues come from unclear expectations set at the start

cards.headline: Managing Revisions
cards.body: Revisions are where projects go off the rails. Set boundaries early and stick to them professionally.
bullets: Include 2 revision rounds in your contract (industry standard)
Define what counts as a revision vs a new direction
Present 2-3 options at concept stage (avoids later pivots)
Use timestamp-based feedback: "At 0:15, change the colour to..."
Additional revisions beyond scope: Quote them immediately

cards.headline: Delivery & File Formats
cards.body: Deliver professionally with all the formats your client needs. This small extra effort creates massive client satisfaction.
bullets: Master file: Full quality MP4 (H.264, 4K or 1080p)
Social formats: 9:16 (Stories/Reels), 1:1 (Feed), 16:9 (YouTube)
Thumbnails: Still frames exported as PNG for each video
Captions: SRT file for accessibility
Delivery: Google Drive or Frame.io link (not email attachments)

cards.headline: Create Your Client Template
cards.body: Build a creative brief template (Google Doc) with sections: Client goals, Target audience, Brand guidelines, Video style, Key messages, Deliverables, Timeline, Revision policy. Use this for every future project.

quiz.question: How many revision rounds should you include in standard client contracts?
quiz.explanation: 1-2 revision rounds is industry standard. It gives clients flexibility while protecting you from endless changes. Additional rounds are quoted separately.

quiz.question: 80% of client issues come from unclear expectations set at the start.
quiz.explanation: Most project problems stem from misaligned expectations. A thorough discovery call and written creative brief prevent the majority of issues.

quiz.question: What is the recommended way to deliver final video files to clients?
quiz.explanation: Cloud links (Google Drive or Frame.io) allow easy access, multiple format downloads, and don't hit email size limits. Professional and convenient.

lessons.title: Your AI Studio Launch Plan
lessons.subtitle: 30-day action plan to go live as an AI filmmaker

cards.headline: From Student to Studio
cards.body: You now have every skill to launch a real AI video business. This final lesson gives you the exact 30-day plan to go from course graduate to earning client.

cards.headline: Week 1: Foundation
cards.body: Set up your professional presence and create your launch assets.
bullets: Day 1-2: Finalise your showreel (30-60 seconds)
Day 3-4: Build your portfolio page (website or Behance)
Day 5: Write your service packages and pricing
Day 6: Set up business essentials (email, invoicing, contract template)
Day 7: Post your showreel on LinkedIn + Instagram

cards.headline: Week 2-3: Outreach & First Clients
cards.body: Actively pursue your first paying clients with a systematic approach.
bullets: Create 5 free sample videos for dream clients (personalised)
Send 10 cold outreach messages per day with samples attached
Post daily AI video content on social media (build authority)
Join relevant communities (Facebook groups, Reddit, Discord)
Offer "launch pricing" — 50% off for your first 3 clients
Follow up on every conversation within 24 hours
cards.statLabel: Days from today to your first paid AI video project

cards.headline: Week 4: Scale & Systematise
cards.body: Turn early wins into a sustainable business system.
bullets: Collect testimonials from first clients (video if possible)
Create templates for repeat project types
Start uploading stock footage (50 clips minimum)
Set up a referral system (offer 10% commission)
Raise prices by 20% after your first 3 projects
Goal: £3,000+ monthly revenue within 90 days

cards.headline: Launch Today
cards.body: Open your calendar. Block time for Week 1 actions starting tomorrow. Create your first free sample video for a local business tonight. Send it with your pitch. Your AI filmmaking studio is officially open for business.

quiz.question: What should you create in Week 1 of your studio launch?
options: Showreel, portfolio, service packages, and business essentials
Wait for clients to come to you
quiz.explanation: Week 1 is about foundations: a professional showreel, portfolio page, clear pricing, and business setup. This gives you credibility before outreach begins.

quiz.question: Offering 50% off "launch pricing" for your first 3 clients is a recommended strategy.
quiz.explanation: Launch pricing reduces risk for early clients, helps you build case studies and testimonials quickly, and gives you real-world experience to justify higher prices later.

quiz.question: What is the revenue goal within 90 days of launching your AI video studio?
quiz.explanation: £3,000+ monthly revenue within 90 days is an achievable target with consistent outreach, a strong portfolio, and multiple income streams (clients + stock footage).
